name: contextforge-capture
description: Automatically captures AI agent conversations and stores them in a knowledge graph via MCP to optimize agent context across sessions. Provided by AdoptNow.AI.
author: Vikas Rai

contextforge.captureDelaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait after last write before considering a session complete

contextforge.minMessages.description: Minimum number of messages required to capture a session

contextforge.binaryPath.description: Path to the ContextForge binary. Leave empty to use ~/.contextforge/contextforge

chatParticipants.name: memory
chatParticipants.description: Query and manage your persistent knowledge graph

commands.name: save
commands.description: Save the current conversation to the knowledge graph

commands.name: search
commands.description: Search the knowledge graph for past work

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show memory status across all workspaces

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_get_workspace_context
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get all known entities, relationships, and facts for a workspace. Use this at the start of a conversation to load relevant context from past work.

workspace.description: Workspace path to get context for

limit.description: Max entities to return. Default: 500. Pass 200 for small contexts, 500 for 128K models, 1000 max for 200K+. Do NOT exceed 1000.

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_search_memory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the knowledge graph for entities (files, functions, libraries, errors, decisions, patterns) and past conversations by semantic similarity. Use this to recall past work, decisions, and context from previous conversations across all workspaces.

query.description: Entity name or partial name to search for. Also searches conversation summaries semantically.

workspace.description: Filter to a specific workspace path

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_save_conversation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Save a completed conversation. Extracts entities, relationships, and facts into the knowledge graph. Raw text is discarded after extraction. Call this when a meaningful conversation ends.

workspace.description: Workspace path where the conversation took place

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_add_fact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Store a specific fact about an entity. Use this to record decisions, patterns, conventions, or other knowledge that should persist.

entityName.description: Name of the entity (file, function, service, etc.)

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_memory_status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show what is stored in the knowledge graph — list of workspaces, entity counts, fact counts, and date ranges. Use this to understand what the agent remembers.

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_cleanup_memory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Delete knowledge from a specific time range. Use this when the user wants to clear recent memory (e.g. 'forget the last 2 hours'). Removes entities, facts, and relationships created within the specified time window.

hours.description: Delete knowledge from the last N hours

workspace.description: Optional: limit cleanup to a specific workspace

languageModelTools.name: contextforge_forget_workspace
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Completely erase all knowledge for a specific workspace. Use this when the user wants a fresh start for a project, or when stored knowledge is outdated/wrong. This is irreversible.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm deletion. This is irreversible.

scripts.package: npm run bundle && npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies
scripts.package:darwin-arm64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=darwin-arm64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target darwin-arm64
scripts.package:darwin-x64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=darwin-x64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target darwin-x64
scripts.package:win32-x64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=win32-x64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target win32-x64
scripts.package:win32-arm64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=win32-arm64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target win32-arm64
scripts.package:linux-x64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=linux-x64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target linux-x64
scripts.package:linux-arm64: CONTEXTFORGE_TARGET=linux-arm64 npm run copy-server && npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target linux-arm64
scripts.package:all: npm run bundle && npm run package:darwin-arm64 && npm run package:darwin-x64 && npm run package:win32-x64 && npm run package:linux-x64 && npm run package:linux-arm64
scripts.dist: npm run fetch-deps && npm run prebundle-server && npm run package:all && node -e "const fs=require('fs'),p=require('path');fs.mkdirSync('../../dist',{recursive:true});fs.readdirSync('.').filter(f=>f.endsWith('.vsix')).forEach(f=>{fs.renameSync(f,p.join('../../dist',f));console.log('  →',f)})" && echo 'All VSIXs moved to dist/'
